To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PPRLM baseline system clearly outperformed the PPR system for language identification in lecture speech, and that the hybrid system combining the strengths of both baseline systems performed best.

(1) the use of lexical information in the PPRLM baseline system improves performance, (2) the use of a hybrid system of the PPR baseline with the PPRLM approach results in better performance than either of the baseline systems and has the same run-time as the PPR baseline, and (3) the hybrid approach is our choice for use in the lecture translator system due to the good performance and the same run-time compared to the PPR system.

the PPRLM baseline system outperforms the baseline PPR system, the PPR system can be improved by using keyword spotting and additional language models, a hybrid system combining both the PPR system and PPRLM system can be built and this hybrid outperforms the pure PPR system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of an efficient language identification system that can be used in our simultaneous lecture transcription system.
the development and evaluation of language identification systems that can be used in a simultaneous lecture translation system.
the development of a hybrid language identification system with a fast and robust run-time and good identification performance for the simultaneous lecture translation system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PPRLM baseline system is a good choice for language identification tasks, but that the hybrid system should be used for the lecture translation application due to its fast processing time.
our PPRLM baseline system is our best choice for language identification in the lecture translation application.
the hybrid system performs the best on all the conditions that we tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to build a fast and accurate language identification system that will be useful for our simultaneous lecture translation application.

we have shown that a hybrid approach combining the advantages of both PPR and PPMLR systems, can outperform the baseline systems and can be used as a fast and reliable front-end language identification component in the lecture translation framework.

the use of lexical features and additional language models in combination with a score-fusing approach for language discrimination and SVM classification for language identification can significantly improve the performance of a phonotactic language model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of phonotactic and lexical language identification approaches can be beneficial for language identification in the presence of speech recognition errors.
a combination of phonotactic and lexical information can lead to better results than using only one type of information.
the use of lexical information in the language identification task is crucial, and that a hybrid of a PPR and PPPLM system can be a very good compromise between performance and run-time.
